item.title: Exploring Covalent Organic Cage as Heterogenous Platform for Aerobic Photooxidation of Alcohols
item.description:
Here, we have developed P2D3R, a metal-free covalent organic cage that uses visible light and molecular oxygen to efficiently oxidize various alcohols. This robust photocatalyst achieves high yields exceeding 90% within minutes and maintains its performance over eight reusable cycles. Its broad substrate scope allows for the gram-scale production of valuable compounds, including the antibacterial and antioxidant agent vanillin. This innovation offers a sustainable, rapid, and scalable approach to green chemical synthesis under mild aerobic conditions.


Innovation of sustainable and efficient catalytic systems for controlled aerobic oxidation of alcohols remains a fundamental challenge in green chemistry. Here, we report a phenothiazine-functionalized covalent organic cage (P 2 D 3 R) as a robust heterogeneous platform for photocatalytic dehydrogenative oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols. The trigonal-prismatic cage was synthesized via [2 + 3] imine condensation followed by reduction. Gas-phase DFT calculations confirmed its shape-persistent architecture and internal confined cavity. Under ambient aerobic conditions, P 2 D 3 R catalyzes the oxidation of various benzyl alcohols to their corresponding benzaldehyde/acetophenone derivatives, under an open atmosphere without any additives or metal-based oxidants. Optimization studies revealed rapid kinetics, high selectivity, and excellent yields under benign conditions. The catalysis demonstrates broad substrate scope for efficiently oxidizing aryl and heteroaryl alcohols bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents with high yields (>90%) and gram-scale scalability within minutes. Moreover, the catalyst is recoverable and reusable over eight cycles without loss of catalytic activity. Notably, two value-added natural products, vanillin and camphor, were obtained from this present catalysis, where vanillin is well known for its antibacterial and antioxidant properties. This work highlights organic cages as a promising porous material for next-generation additive-free photocatalysts, integrating light harvesting, substrate confinement, and recyclability within discrete multifunctional systems.

item.title: Synthesis of S‐Arylthioxanthonium Trifluoromethanesulfonates From Thioxanthones and Diaryliodonium Salts by Copper(II) Catalysis and Application to Aryl–Heteroaryl Bond Formation by Direct LED Irradiation
item.description:
A straightforward Cu(II)-catalyzed synthesis of S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonates from readily available thioxanthones and diaryliodonium salts is described. A broad range of salts is obtained in moderate to good yields. It is further demonstrated that S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonates act as aryl radical precursors under simple direct 365-nm LED irradiation, enabling aryl–heteroaryl bond formation without any metal-based photocatalyst.


A short and versatile route to S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonates via a Cu-catalyzed reaction of diaryliodonium trifluoromethanesulfonates and commercially available thioxanthones is described. Variously substituted S-arylthioxanthonium salts were prepared in only one step from diaryliodonium salts in moderate to good yields. Then, we show one of the first applications of an S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonate, as an efficient aryl radical precursor by simple and mild direct 365-nm LED irradiation. In preliminary experiments, this aryl radical was successfully trapped with furan without any metallic photocatalyst, thereby enabling the first formation of a new aryl–heteroaryl bond from a sulfonium salt derived from thioxanthone.

item.title: Sustainable Catalyst‐Free Synthesis of Substituted Pyrazoles Through an Annulation/Oxidation Cascade Under Batch and Continuous‐Flow Methods
item.description:
This method enables a sustainable, catalyst-free synthesis of highly functionalized pyrazoles via a formal [3 + 2] annulation-oxidation approach in batch and continuous-flow conditions.


We describe a catalyst-free synthesis of substituted pyrazoles in good to excellent yields using α,β-unsaturated β-ketoesters and aryl hydrazines under mild reaction conditions. The reaction proceeds through a Michael-initiated ring closure reaction followed by in situ oxidation. A broad range of substrates bearing electron-withdrawing and electron-donating substituents was successfully converted to the corresponding pyrazole derivatives. The method was scalable under batch conditions, demonstrating its practical applicability. In addition, the ester group present in the products could be transformed into the corresponding carboxylic acid and amide derivatives, providing access to structurally diverse pyrazole scaffolds. The protocol was also translated to continuous-flow conditions, offering an efficient and sustainable route to these valuable heterocyclic compounds.

item.title: Synthesis of Naphthoquinones by Pd‐Catalyzed Heck–Matsuda Arylation of Lapachol
item.description:
Direct Heck–Matsuda arylation of lapachol enables the efficient synthesis of diverse naphthoquinones under homogeneous and heterogeneous palladium catalysis. The methodology features broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and provides a practical platform for quinone diversification.


Direct Heck–Matsuda arylation of lapachol provides rapid access to structurally diverse naphthoquinones under homogeneous and heterogeneous palladium catalysis. The methodology features broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and unambiguous structural assignment by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, providing an efficient platform for the diversification of quinones.

item.title: Azole‐Fused High‐Energy Heterocycles: A Decade of Synthetic Innovation and Structure–Property Insights (2015–2025)
item.description:
This review summarizes progress reported since 2015 on 97 azole-fused energetic heterocycles, including synthetic routes, density, detonation performance, thermal stability, and mechanical sensitivity. Representative advances in fused-ring construction and functionalization are summarized, while key strategic challenges in synthesizing complex fused nitrogen-rich frameworks and simultaneously achieving balanced overall performance are highlighted.


As modern weaponry and equipment evolve, there is an increasing demand for more powerful, less sensitive, and environmentally benign energetic materials. Fused heterocycle-based energetic materials, large conjugated systems composed of two or more rings that share adjacent atoms, exhibit superior thermal stability and higher density than their monocyclic and bridged analogs. Meanwhile, similar to cage heterocyclic rings, the fused structures generally possess higher heats of formation and elevated ring-strain energies, which enhance detonation performance. In addition, the fused backbones offer versatile modification sites, enabling researchers to balance energy and stability by introducing different functional groups. This review summarizes the research progress on 97 energetic fused heterocyclic compounds from the Web of Science (WOS) and Scopus databases since 2015 and presents their molecular design strategies, synthesis methods, and detonation properties. Furthermore, the major challenges are associated with the design of complex fused-ring frameworks and the large-scale preparation. This review highlights the insightful future research directions, particularly the development of universal synthesis strategies and the exploration of AI-driven automated design.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Hydroxylation of Simple Fluoroaryl and Aryl Chlorides: A Route to (Fluoro)phenols
item.description:
A copper-catalyzed conversion of simple polyfluoroaryl chlorides to the corresponding phenols was developed. A simple ligand system was applied, as well as potassium carbonate as an inexpensive and effective base, while significantly suppressing competing SNAr pathways. Use of a sulfolane/water solvent system enabled high reactivity at a low catalyst loading, underscoring the practicality and scalability of this protocol.


A copper-catalyzed conversion of polyfluoroaryl chlorides to the corresponding phenols was developed. A simple ligand system was applied, as well as potassium carbonate as an inexpensive and effective base, while significantly suppressing competing SNAr pathways. The generality of the method was further demonstrated with simple aryl chlorides, which also underwent efficient hydroxylation. Mechanistic studies suggest that the reaction proceeds via a Cu(I)/Cu(III) catalytic cycle. Notably, the use of a sulfolane/water solvent system enabled high reactivity at a low catalyst loading, underscoring the practicality and scalability of this protocol.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Benzimidazole‐Fused Phenanthridines and Quinolines
item.description:
Benzimidazole-fused phenanthridines and quinolines are constructed by copper-catalyzed C(sp2)─C and C(sp2)─N couplings between 2-(2-bromoaryl)benzimidazoles/2-(2-bromovinyl)benzimidazoles and 2-bromoarylboronic acids under microwave irradiation.


A modular synthetic method for benzimidazole-fused phenanthridines, benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-f]phenanthridines, has been developed via copper-catalyzed sequential C(sp2)─C and C(sp2)─N bond formations between 2-(2-bromoaryl)benzimidazoles and 2-bromoarylboronic acids under microwave irradiation. The construction of benzimidazole-fused quinolines, benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a]quinolines, is also achieved by treating 2-(2-bromovinyl)benzimidazoles with 2-bromophenylboronic acid under similar copper catalysis. A control experiment indicates the involvement of competing copper-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura-type C─C and Ullmann-type C─N coupling pathways.

item.title: The Expanding Role of Diazirines in Synthetic Methodology
item.description:
Beyond their established role in photoaffinity labeling, diazirines have emerged as versatile reagents in synthetic chemistry. This review highlights their dual reactivity as carbene and nitrogen-transfer precursors, showcasing mechanistic insights and diverse applications in cyclopropanations, cycloadditions, skeletal editing, amination, heterocycle synthesis, and related transformations.


Diazirines are three-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycles best known as photochemical carbene precursors in photoaffinity labeling. Upon irradiation, diazirines undergo nitrogen extrusion to generate highly reactive carbenes capable of covalent bond insertion, a property that has been widely exploited in chemical biology and materials science. Despite their favorable handling properties compared to related diazo compounds and their versatility as both carbene precursors and nitrogen sources, diazirines have historically seen only limited application in synthetic organic chemistry. Over the past two decades, however, diazirines have increasingly emerged as valuable synthons in a broad range of transformations. Their applications can generally be divided into reactions exploiting either their carbene-generating properties or their ability to serve as nitrogen-transfer reagents. Diazirines have been employed in cyclopropanation and cyclopropenation reactions, cross-couplings, skeletal editing, glycosylations, reductive aminations, and the synthesis of nitrogen-containing heterocycles. Owing to their unique reactivity, diazirines can facilitate unusual or otherwise difficult-to-access transformations in organic synthesis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of diazirine-based synthetic methodologies, with particular emphasis on developments reported over the last two decades, and highlights future opportunities for their application in organic synthesis.

item.title: 2‐Fluoroanthraquinone‐Catalyzed Photooxidation of Benzylic Hydrocarbons and Aliphatic Alcohols With O2 in Supercritical CO2, Accelerating Effect of Water
item.description:
A greener method for photocatalytic oxidation of benzylic hydrocarbons and aliphatic alcohols with O2 in supercritical CO2 medium under blue light irradiation was developed using 2-fluoroanthraquinone (2-FAQ) as a metal-free catalyst. The excited-state redox potential of 2-FAQ was determined. The promoting effect of water additives is discovered, so the plausible oxidation mechanisms with participation of water are discussed.


A greener process for the oxidation of hydrocarbons containing primary, secondary, and tertiary benzylic carbon atoms, as well as aliphatic alcohols (e.g., cyclohexanol, menthol, and 4-heptanol) with molecular oxygen in supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO2) medium under the visible-light irradiation in the presence of 2-fluoroanthraquinone (2-FAQ) as a photocatalyst (1 mol%) has been developed. The photooxidation reactions have been found to be accelerated by the addition of small amounts (1 equiv.) of water to the system. Plausible pathways for the promotion of the oxidation process have been identified: The most prominent is the cleavage of H─O bonds in the added water molecules under the action of the photocatalyst that results in extra reactive oxygen species generation. Also, a radical-chain mechanism for the photocatalytic process has been proposed. It is the first time that experimental data on the photophysical properties of 2-FAQ, including the redox potential of this promising photocatalyst in the photoexcited state, have been obtained.

item.title: Conversion of Alcohols to Alkyl Chlorides Using the Bichloride Ionic Liquid [NEt3Me][Cl(HCl)n]
item.description:
The ionic liquid [NEt3Me][Cl(HCl)1.61] is presented as a controllable source of HCl for the effective transformation of a broad range of alcohols into alkyl chlorides. The process eliminates the need for continuous handling of HCl gas and enables a recyclable IL-based catalyst system.


The solvent-free chlorination of alcohols using the bichloride-based ionic liquid [NEt3Me][Cl(HCl)1.61] as a hydrogen chloride source is reported. In the presence of a catalytic amount of a carboxylic acid, a variety of alcohols undergo efficient chlorination under mild batch conditions. This method eliminates the need to handle hydrogen chloride gas. Benzyl and secondary alcohols are converted with good to excellent yields, whereas primary aliphatic substrates show moderate reactivity. Notably, short-chain diol substrates primarily yield monochlorinated products, indicating some chemoselectivity under the reaction conditions. Tests for functional group compatibility reveal that ester groups stay intact, while acetals and simple alkyl ethers are cleaved in the strongly acidic environment. The ionic liquid can be recharged with hydrogen chloride and reused in subsequent reactions. Process robustness is demonstrated by gram-scale reactions and straightforward product isolation via distillation or phase separation.

item.title: Developing a p‐Toluenesulfonic Acid/Benzenesulfonic Acid/Water Mixture as Sustainable Medium for Aqueous Diels–Alder Reactions of Hydrophobic Anthracenes and Various Dienophiles
item.description:
Classic Diels–Alder reactions generally require anhydrous organic solvents, resulting in significant solvent waste. Herein, we established an aqueous Diels–Alder reaction by using acidic hydrotropes to generate a sustainable medium. The method features good functional group compatibility of various dienophiles and excellent solvent recyclability, providing various bridged cycloadducts in excellent yield.


Aqueous Diels–Alder reactions are highly attractive for green chemistry because of their 100% atom economy and solvent waste mitigation. Despite significant effort, reactions involving hydrophobic dienes and water-sensitive dienophiles, or vice versa, remain challenging. Herein, we implemented an efficient Diels–Alder reaction in a mixture of aqueous p-toluenesulfonic acid and benzenesulfonic acid as a recyclable medium. The methodology features good compatibility with hydrophobic anthracenes and water-sensitive dienophiles, excellent yields, and chromatography-free product isolation. The aqueous medium could easily be recovered and reused multiple times without additional processing.

item.title: Hydrosilylation of Nitrones With Trichlorosilane: Preparation of Hydroxylamines
item.description:
An inherent directing group enabled hydrosilylation of nitrones with trichlorosilane has been unprecedentedly developed, providing an efficient and transition metal-free method for the synthesis of hydroxylamines.


Herein, we describe a novel catalyst- and transition-metal-free method for the hydrosilylation of nitrones with trichlorosilane. A variety of hydroxylamines (38 examples) were obtained in moderate to good yields (28%–88%) with broad substrate compatibility under mild and operationally simple conditions. Control experiments confirm that the inherent directing groups of nitrones plays a pivotal role in bridging the reactants and facilitating the reaction. Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis and elaboration of the products.

item.title: Substituent‐Driven Selective Functionalization of Dibromovinyl‐Aromatics/Heteroaromatics to Give Esters and/or Terminal Alkynes
item.description:
Room-temperature transformations of 1,1-dibromoalkenes for the generation of esters and terminal alkynes with the aid of sodium alkoxide. Electronic factors of substituents play a crucial role in determining the reaction pathway and result in divergent synthesis.


Interesting room-temperature transformations of aryl/heteroaryl-substituted 1,1-dibromoalkenes have been developed for the generation of esters and terminal alkynes with the aid of sodium alkoxides, which are triggered by the electronic effects of the aryl/heteroaryl ring. The group attached to the aryl ring plays a crucial role in determining the reaction pathway; in general, electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) direct the reaction to the formation of esters. On the other hand, electron-donating groups (EDG) on the ring turn the reaction in another direction to produce terminal alkynes.

item.title: Lipase‐Mediated Selective Synthesis of Aldopentofuranoses
item.description: The selective modification of carbohydrates using enzymatic approaches has attracted significant interest for its efficiency, specificity and sustainability. In our study, we systematically examined the conversion of aldopentoses to their corresponding furanose derivatives using immobilised Candida antarctica lipase B (NVZ-435) and vinyl benzoate, exploring various solvents and reaction times. The 5-O-mono-protected furanoses of seven d- and l-aldopentoses were obtained with yields up to 100%. In cases where lower yields were observed, such as with d-arabinofuranose and l-lyxofuranose, the 2,5- and 1,5-O-dibenzoylated furanosyl products were obtained in 73% and 40% yield, respectively. These findings broaden the scope of biocatalysis as a selective, sustainable and highly efficient approach for challenging carbohydrate synthesis.

item.title: Development of Optically Active Amino Acids Containing Tetraphenylmethane Core
item.description:
From a geometric perspective, treating adamantane and tetraphenylmethane as large analogs of methane enables the creation of chiral amino acids based on these structures. Following the development of optically active amino acids containing an adamantane core, this study focused on developing new amino acids containing a tetraphenylmethane core. These amino acids can be utilized as novel chiral building blocks that do not undergo racemization.


The synthesis of novel amino acids containing a tetraphenylmethane core was achieved by employing the Friedel–Crafts alkylation reaction between a triarylmethyl cation and aniline as the key reaction. Optical resolution of one of the racemic products was achieved by preparative HPLC using a chiral stationary phase column, and the absolute configuration of one enantiomer was determined by X-ray crystallography. The optically active amino acids can be utilized as novel chiral building blocks. To demonstrate this, the synthesis of an optically active Pd complex was carried out. Furthermore, in the context of applications in digital polymers, the synthesis of a tripeptide with methane, adamantane, and tetraphenylmethane cores was also achieved.

item.title: Photocatalytic Radical Addition to N1‐Allenyl Benzimidazoles: A Metal‐Free Route to Sulfonylated Benzimidazoles
item.description:
A visible-light-mediated, metal-free radical addition of sodium sulfinates to N1-allenyl benzimidazoles is reported. This mild protocol efficiently constructs novel sulfonylated benzimidazole derivatives, addressing the scarcity of N-heterocyclic allenamides and expanding access to bioactive scaffolds.


A metal-free, visible-light-driven radical sulfonylation of N1-allenyl benzimidazoles with sodium sulfinates has been developed. Under mild photoredox conditions, a diverse array of aryl, heteroaryl, and aliphatic sulfinates efficiently couple with allenamide substrates to afford structurally diverse sulfonylated benzimidazoles in good to excellent yields. Mechanistic studies support a radical-mediated pathway initiated by the single-electron oxidation of the sulfinate anion. The transformation demonstrates excellent scalability to gram quantities without compromising efficiency. This operationally simple, transition-metal-free protocol offers a sustainable and versatile strategy for accessing biologically relevant sulfonylated heterocycles.

item.title: Direct CH Bond Halogenation of Cubane Skeleton Mediated by Photocatalysis
item.description:
H Bond Halogenation of Cubane Skeleton Mediated by Photocatalysis"/>

A visible-light photo-induced direct halogenation of cubane CH bonds has been developed via a photocatalytic hydrogen atom transfer strategy, and the chloro-, bromo-, and iodo-substituted cubane derivatives have been obtained in poor-to-excellent yields. The substrates scope of different halogenation reactions was investigated.


The synthesis of multisubstituted cubane derivatives remains challenging due to the limitations of current synthetic methods. Therefore, developing site-selective CH halogenation reactions starting from simple 1,4-substituted cubane compounds is highly desirable. Herein, we report an efficient strategy for the CH halogenation of cubane using sodium decatungstate (NaDT) as a hydrogen atom transfer photocatalyst to produce cubyl radicals which could undergo halogenation with different halogen sources to achieve chloro-, bromo-, and iodo-substituted cubane derivatives in poor-to-excellent yields ranging from 12% to 94%. This method offers a practical route for accessing multifunctionalized cubanes for further research.

item.title: 1,4‐Dithianes in Synthesis: Rapid Assembly of Indolizidine Alkaloid‐Type Scaffolds Through Cationic Polyene Cyclization
item.description:
A practical three-step assembly process is reported for the synthesis of a few substituted indolizidine scaffolds starting from commercial starting materials. The synthetic steps are aided by a strategic 1,4-dithiane ring fused to a simple maleimide building block.


We report a synthetic approach to the indolizidine scaffold, fused to a 1,4-dithiane. In a straightforward three-step protocol, the commercially available building block 5,6-dihydro-1,4-dithiin-2,3-dicarboximide undergoes two consecutive alkenylations, followed by a cationic cyclization mediated by an α,β-unsaturated N-acyliminium ion, affording a small range of substituted indolizidine scaffolds. The reaction was originally observed as an unexpected side reaction, but offers an attractive entry into this class of biologically active alkaloids.

item.title: Air‐Oxidative Synthesis of Diaryl Ketones From Aryl Acetonitrile and Aryl Halides via Single‐Electron Transfer
item.description:
A one-pot, two-step method has been developed for the synthesis of diaryl ketones under basic conditions, using aryl halides and aryl acetonitriles as substrates, without the use of metals or Lewis acids.


Under base-mediated conditions, the synthesis of diaryl ketones is accomplished through a one-pot, two-step process that utilizes aryl halides and aryl acetonitriles as substrates. This method finds application in the synthesis of aryl iodides, bromides, and specific aryl chlorides. Mechanistic studies indicate that the Cs2CO3/DMSO system induces the formation of an aryl radical, which reacts with dehydrogenated acetonitrile via a single-electron transfer (SET) reaction. Subsequently, under the action of oxygen in air, oxidation occurs, leading to the cleavage of the CCN bond and rearrangement, thereby forming diaryl ketone.

item.title: Chemoselective Deprotection of Levulinic Ester (Lev) With Ethanolic KOH‐2‐MeTHF: A Green Alternative to Hydrazinolysis
item.description:
A green, sustainable, chemoselective deprotection of levulinic ester using ethanolic KOH in 2-MeTHF has been established. This safe, mild, and efficient deprotection method works at ambient temperature.


Herein, we report a potassium hydroxide-mediated chemoselective deprotection of levulinic ester (Lev) in 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF) in the presence of various functionalities at ambient temperature. This mild deprotection protocol, using cost-effective and safe-to-handle reagents, is scalable and useful for deprotecting levulinic ester (Lev) in complex molecules such as steroids, amino acids, and carbohydrates in the presence of various functionalities/protecting groups. This approach would be an excellent alternative to hydrazinolysis, which poses significant safety and environmental concerns.

item.title: One‐Pot Shotgun Synthesis of Earring‐Shaped and Jaw‐Like Porphyrin Macrocycles
item.description:
From a single β-borylated Ni(II) porphyrin precursor, a one-pot platinum-mediated macrocyclization yields three earring-shaped monoporhyrins (ER2–ER4) with different bridge lengths and a jaw-like dimer (JW), demonstrating a divergent strategy for accessing strained porphyrin macrocycles.


A one-pot, shotgun platinum-mediated macrocyclization strategy for the synthesis of earring-shaped and jaw-like porphyrin macrocycles is reported. From the coupling of a 2,12-diborylated Ni(II) porphyrin precursor with excess bis(4-borylphenyl)methane, three earring-shaped monoporphyrins (ER2, ER3, and ER4) bearing bridges of two, three, and four bis(4-phenylene)methane units, along with a jaw-like dimer (JW) featuring two independent bridges at the 2-2′ and 18-18′ positions, were obtained in a single reaction. 1H NMR spectroscopy reveals a progressive downfield shift of the meso protons as the bridge length increases from ER2 to ER4, consistent with gradual release of ring strain. The X-ray structure of JW confirms a curved jaw-like geometry with a dihedral angle of 119.65° between the two porphyrin planes, and the two porphyrin rings exhibit distinct degrees of saddle-shaped distortion. UV/Vis absorption shows a large bathochromic shift from ER4 to ER3 (12 nm) but only a marginal shift from ER3 to ER2 (1 nm). This work demonstrates that divergent one-pot cyclization is a powerful strategy for accessing strained porphyrin macrocycles with different ring sizes and architectures, providing an efficient platform for systematic structure–property studies.

item.title: Synthesis of Ionizable Lipid ALC‐0315 Using Hydrogen Borrowing Catalysis
item.description:
A hydrogen borrowing catalytic method based on a well-established Ir-catalyst was applied for a streamlined gram-scale synthesis of the ionizable lipid, ALC-0315, used in Pfizer/BioNtech SARS-CoV-19 vaccine. The methodology enabled several-fold improvements in overall yields and enhanced step economy without the use of highly toxic reagents and is also broadly applicable to more challenging asymmetric lipids.


The ionizable lipid ALC-0315 was one of the crucial compounds that made the Pfizer/BioNtech COVID-19 mRNA vaccine successful. Herein, we developed an Ir-catalyzed approach where both the fatty aldehyde synthesis and the double reductive amination proceed simultaneously in a one-pot approach. Using this hydrogen borrowing catalysis methodology, we have multiplied the yields of ALC-0315 compared to the original process and improved step economy without the use of highly toxic reagents. As the second alkylation step in the Ir catalysis is much slower, the strategy is also amenable to asymmetric lipids, which can be challenging via other methods.

item.title: Synthesis and Structural Study of Iodonium Ylides Derived From 2‐Iodosylbenzenesulfonic Acid: Reagents for Preparation of Annulated Thiazoles
item.description:
New ylides of two different types were prepared by reaction of 2-iodosylbenzenesulfonic acid with the corresponding 1,3-cyclohexanediones under acidic or basic conditions. These compounds have a typical for iodonium ylides structure with the CIC angles 94.18° –97.25° and the IC bond distances between 2.08 and 2.13 Å. The new bench-stable ylides are useful reagents for the preparation of annulated thiazoles by cycloaddition reaction with thiourea.


Novel ylidic compounds of two different types have been prepared by the reaction of 2-iodosylbenzenesulfonic acid with the corresponding 1,3-cyclohexanediones under acidic or basic conditions. According to X-ray crystallographic study, these compounds have a typical for iodonium ylide structure with two carbon atoms bonding to the iodine atom with the CIC angles ranging from 94.18° to 97.25° and the IC bond distances about 2.08 (I–Calkyl) and 2.13 Å (I–Caryl). Numerous inter- and intramolecular halogen bonding interactions were observed and analyzed. In contrast to the known dimedone-derived phenyliodonium ylides, these new iodonium ylides are generally stable compounds with high decomposition temperatures and stable for handling and storage at room temperature. The new iodonium ylides are useful reagents for the preparation of annulated thiazoles by cycloaddition reaction with thiourea.

item.title: Building Blocks for Acetylenic Scaffolding Inspired by 6,6,12‐Graphyne
item.description:
6,6,12-Graphyne is an elusive allotrope of carbon. Here, we present the synthesis and properties of a selection of useful molecular building blocks to advance the preparation of various segments of 6,6,12-graphyne. These modules are derived from tri- and tetraethynylethene derivatives, di- and tetraethynyl-substituted tolane derivatives, as well as cyclic dehydroannulene and radiaannulene derivatives with peripheral alkyne substituents.


Acetylenic scaffolding is a synthetic method for the preparation of large, carbon-rich frameworks using acetylenic coupling reactions. Segments of the elusive carbon allotrope 6,6,12-graphyne present acetylenic frameworks that are particularly challenging to synthesize. Here, we present the development of a variety of molecular building blocks to advance the synthesis of such segments. The modules are derived from tri- and tetraethynylethene derivatives, di- and tetraethynyl-substituted tolane derivatives, and cyclic dehydroannulene and radiaannulene derivatives with peripheral alkyne substituents. The compounds were prepared by a combination of selective desilylation of trialkylsilyl-protected enyne compounds and Sonogashira coupling reactions of the terminal alkynes with suitable aryl or vinyl halides. One example involves a novel and simple synthesis of tetra-substituted tetraethynylethenes in the cis configuration from a readily available starting material; such compounds have hitherto required a multistep and tedious protocol to prepare. Moreover, aluminum chloride-mediated conversion of trimethylsilyl-substituted terminal alkynes into ketone functionalities upon treatment with acid chloride substrates is presented as a convenient way of achieving useful building blocks. Intramolecular cyclization via a McMurry coupling of the dione allowed the ready synthesis of a functionalized dehydroannulene, presenting an alternative to the Sonogashira cyclization approaches used previously to form this core.

item.title: Infrared Irradiation‐Assisted Pd/Cu Catalysis for Sustainable C–N Cross‐Coupling Reactions
item.description:
A combined Pd/Cu catalytic system is demonstrated to be highly effective in promoting infrared irradiation-assisted Buchwald–Hartwig aminations under nonanhydrous and open-air conditions, using only a stoichiometric amount of a green reaction solvent. The C–N coupling reactions were performed with aryl halides bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents, along with a variety of secondary amines.


Herein, a practical and efficient Pd/Cu-catalyzed Buchwald–Hartwig amination under infrared irradiation is reported. The reaction proceeds under quasi-solvent-free, nonanhydrous conditions and without the need for an inert atmosphere, using only a stoichiometric amount of the green solvent cyclopentyl methyl ether (CPME) as the reaction medium. The cooperative Pd/Cu catalytic system, combined with near-infrared irradiation centered at 1.2 μm, enables high-yield C–N couplings of aryl iodides and bromides with a variety of secondary amines with a reduced palladium loading (1.5 mol%) and in short reaction times (1–3 h). Overall, this protocol provides a rapid, sustainable, and broadly applicable route to aryl amines, affording good to excellent yields (68%–99%) under operationally simple conditions.

item.title: Diphenyl Disulfide‐Promoted Racemization of 1‐Arylethanols for Photobiocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolution
item.description:
Purple-light activation of aggregated diphenyl disulfide unlocks the photocatalyst-free racemization of 1-arylethanols. The resulting sulfur radical process operates under mild conditions and couples with the enzymatic acylation by Candida antarctica lipase B in a photobiocatalytic dynamic kinetic resolution, revealing new opportunities for sulfur radicals in hybrid catalysis.


We report a photocatalyst-free racemization of 1-arylethanols using substoichiometric diphenyl disulfide under purple light irradiation. Spectroscopic and computational studies suggest aggregation-enabled activation of the disulfide. The preliminary integration with Candida antarctica lipase B into a photobiocatalytic dynamic kinetic resolution on electron-rich 1-arylethanols, highlights the potential of sulfur radical chemistry in hybrid catalytic systems.

item.title: Room‐Temperature Synthesis of C2‐Unsubstituted 2‐Imino‐1,3,4‐oxadiazolines by Cyclization of N‐Acyldiazenes With Trimethylsilyl Cyanide
item.description:
A transition-metal-free procedure is described for the preparation of C2-unsubstituted 2-imino-1,3,4-oxadiazolines at room temperature by treating N-acyldiazenes with trimethylsilyl cyanide in the presence of tetramethylguanidine. Under optimized conditions, the target products are furnished in 28%–72% yield with broad substrate tolerance for aromatic/heterocyclic groups. A gram-scale synthesis in 70% yield confirmed the scalability of the method.


Herein, a mild and efficient protocol for the construction of 2-imino-1,3,4-oxadiazolines bearing a free N─H bond at the C2-position has been established under ambient conditions. The cyclization reaction readily proceeds between readily available N-acyldiazenes and trimethylsilyl cyanide (TMSCN) with the promotion of tetramethylguanidine (TMG), furnishing a series of structurally diverse products in yields up to 72%. This approach features transition-metal-free conditions, operational simplicity, short reaction time (3–4 h), and gram-scale scalability without obvious erosion of yield.

item.title: Front Cover: Diphenyl Disulfide‐Promoted Racemization of 1‐Arylethanols for Photobiocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolution (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 32/2026)
item.description: The Front Cover illustrates two sides of a river representing the fields of photocatalysis (purple tulips) and biocatalysis (blue tulips), united by a bridge to symbolise their integration into photo-biocatalysis. The insets reveal the key catalysts: an aggregated diphenyl disulfide species, whose enhanced visible-light absorption promotes thiyl radical formation under purple irradiation, enabling the deracemization process (left), and Candida antarctica lipase B catalysing the kinetic resolution of the secondary alcohol (right). More information can be found in the Research Article by C. Guolo, S. Parisotto and C. Prandi (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70724).

item.title: Amidines as Directing Group in CH Activation and Their Application in Medicinal, and Materials Chemistry
item.description:
H Activation and Their Application in Medicinal, and Materials Chemistry"/>

In this review, we have summarized a wide range of synthetic transformations for the rapid and efficient construction of highly substituted fused N-heterocyclic scaffolds from amidine scaffolds via C–H activation. In addition, the medicinal and materials science applications of amidines have also been discussed.


Amidine compounds have extensive applications in biological science because of their ability to form noncovalent interactions with DNA molecular targets and proteins Also, their unique structural and electronic properties allow them to be used as organobases, organocatalysts, ligands for metal-catalyzed reactions, and synthetic building blocks for designing a large class of different synthetic heterocyclic compounds. As a result of their importance, much research has been conducted on developing efficient methods of synthesizing amidines, including ways to selectively functionalize CH and CN bonds on amidine molecules. In addition to their significant biological activities such as anticancer, antiviral, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, antithrombotic, neuroprotective, and antifungal properties, their distinctive physicochemical properties have facilitated their application in materials science, particularly in areas such as optoelectronic devices, CO2 capture, energy-storage systems, ion sensing, and corrosion protection. This review highlights recent developments in the synthesis and functionalization of amidines via CH activation and discusses their emerging roles in medicinal and materials chemistry.

item.title: Retro‐Hetero‐Michael Addition Strategies in Organic Synthesis
item.description:
In this review, synthetic approaches to carbo- and heterocyclic compounds, including natural products, published in the last 15 years (2011–2025) which have either relied upon or included a retro-hetero-Michael addition step at any stage are discussed. The review covers the applications of retro-aza-, retro-oxa-, and retro-thia-Michael addition reactions, which together account for most of the examples that have appeared in the literature.


This review covers the applications of retro-hetero-Michael addition reactions in organic synthesis that have appeared in the literature in the last 15 years, with a focus on the synthesis and modification of carbo- and heterocyclic compounds, including natural products. The retro-aza-, retro-oxa-, and retro-thia-Michael addition reactions which are dealt with in the review have been widely exploited in synthetic organic chemistry to perform functional group manipulation, controlled isomerization, isomeric amplification, racemization for dynamic kinetic resolution, intramolecular rearrangements, and ring opening/ring reconstruction sequences. The syntheses of many complex natural products have included a retro-hetero-Michael addition step at some stage. Thus, what was once considered a problem has now become an established tool in the hands of organic chemists, who can leverage the retro-hetero-Michael addition-based strategies for the preparation of intermediates in the synthesis of natural and biologically active carbo- and heterocyclic compounds.

item.title: Catalytic Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral Indole‐Fused Medium and Large Rings: A Burgeoning Field
item.description:
This review summarizes recent advances in the catalytic enantioselective synthesis of chiral indole-fused medium and large rings. It focuses on key synthetic strategies, underlying reaction mechanisms, catalytic models, and the potential applications of the products. In addition, remaining challenges and future directions are discussed, with the aim of inspiring continued innovation and development in this emerging field.


Chiral indole-fused medium and large rings are key structural motifs prevalent in a diverse array of natural products, chiral catalysts, and pharmaceutically active compounds. Despite their significance, the catalytic enantioselective construction of these ring systems remains a formidable and underexplored challenge. In response, chemists have recently devised innovative strategies that are propelling the rapid emergence of this field, affording novel scaffolds with promising applications in medicinal chemistry and asymmetric catalysis. This review provides a concise yet comprehensive overview of the latest advances in the catalytic enantioselective synthesis of chiral indole-fused medium and large rings. Emphasis is placed on the underlying synthetic strategies, reaction mechanisms, catalytic models, and the potential applications of the resulting products. Furthermore, an outlook on the remaining challenges and future directions is presented to inspire continued innovation in this evolving field and related disciplines.

item.title: Advances in the Study of Visible‐Light‐Mediated Reactions of Thianthrenium Salts
item.description:
In recent years, the reactions of thianthrenium salts in visible light mediation have attracted extensive attention from chemists. Innovative advances have been made in the last 3 years of related research. In this paper, we focus on three mechanisms, photoredox catalysis, energy transfer photocatalysis, and electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes to outline the research on the application of thianthrenium salts in visible photocatalytic reactions from 2022 to 2025.


In recent years, the reactions of thianthrenium salts under visible-light mediation have garnered extensive attention from chemists. Substantial innovative advances have been achieved in related research over the past 3 years. In this paper, we focus on three mechanisms, namely, photoredox catalysis, energy transfer photocatalysis, and electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, to outline the research regarding the applications of thianthrenium salts in visible-light photocatalytic reactions spanning 2022–2025.

item.title: Microwave‐Assisted Copper‐Mediated One‐Pot Sequential Synthesis of Quinolino[3,4‐b]quinoxalines
item.description:
A microwave-assisted CuI-mediated one-pot tandem annulation enables rapid and scalable synthesis of quinolino[3,4-b]quinoxalines from 2-(2-bromophenyl)quinoxalines with aldehydes or benzyl alcohols using TMSN3, affording diverse products in up to 91% yield.


An efficient microwave-assisted one-pot protocol has been developed for the synthesis of 6-aryl/heteroarylquinolino[3,4-‍b]quinoxaline derivatives. The method involves a CuI-mediated tandem annulation of 2-(2-bromophenyl)quinoxalines with aryl and heteroaryl aldehydes, using TMSN3 as the nitrogen source. The transformation proceeds rapidly under microwave irradiation, delivering the desired products in moderate-to-excellent yields (up to 91%) with broad substrate scope. Further, benzyl alcohols (with TBHP) also serve as viable precursors under identical conditions to afford 6-aryl/heteroaryl-quinolino[3,4-b]quinoxaline derivatives. Notably, the protocol eliminates the requirement for a stoichiometric amount of reducing agent used in the earlier protocol. It can be extended to gram-scale synthesis with a remarkably reduced reaction time. Mechanistic investigations, supported by control experiments, ESI-HRMS analysis, and DFT calculations, provide insight into the reaction pathway. This approach offers a rapid, practical, and scalable route to quinolino[3,4-b]quinoxaline frameworks of potential medicinal relevance.

item.title: Recent Advances in CH Bond Functionalization Using Traceless N‐Functionalized Directing Groups
item.description:
H Bond Functionalization Using Traceless N-Functionalized Directing Groups"/>

This review focuses on the development of diverse traceless N-functionalized directing groups and their application in the CH bond functionalization. Typical examples that use N-functionalized TDGs, such as N-oxides, nitrones, N-nitroso groups, hydrazyl groups, N-acyl groups, and other nitrogen-functionalized groups, have been documented in this review.


The chelation-assisted CH bond activation with proper directing groups not only promotes the reaction efficiency but also enables selective CC or CX bond formation at the specific positions. Among them, the traceless directing groups (TDGs) strategy is highly attractive since it allows the in situ removal of directing groups after the directed CH bond functionalization. On the other hand, N-containing substrates, e.g., N-heterocycles, amines, and oximes, are of great importance in both organic synthesis and drug discovery. The directed site-selective CH bond functionalization of nitrogen-based substrates using TDG strategy constitutes an ideal solution to access more elaborate molecules. In this context, this review focus on the development of diverse traceless N-functionalized directing groups and their application in the CH bond functionalization, along with mechanistic insights into the directing group removal steps. Typical examples that use N-functionalized TDGs, such as N-oxides, nitrones, N-nitroso groups, hydrazyl groups, N-acyl groups, and other nitrogen-functionalized groups, have been documented in this review, aiming to give a timely comprehensive overview and stimulate the development of more efficient methodologies.

item.title: Synthesis, Structure, and Physicochemical Properties of Doubly Fused Phenoxazine‐Embedded Dithiasapphyrins
item.description:
Novel doubly fused phenoxazine-embedded dithiasapphyrins were synthesized via an acid-catalyzed (3 + 2) condensation reaction. X-ray crystallographic analysis revealed an unusual bithiophene ring inversion and the formation of two fused tripentacyclic rings within the macrocyclic framework.


Herein, we report the synthesis of a new class of doubly fused phenoxazine-embedded dithiasapphyrins via (3 + 2) condensation of an appropriate phenoxazine-based tripyrrane with bithiophene diol in CH2Cl2 under BF3·OEt2-catalyzed conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis of one representative macrocycle revealed an unusual structural rearrangement involving inversion of the two thiophene rings of the bithiophene unit, followed by fusion of the inner thiophene carbon atoms with adjacent pyrrolic nitrogen atoms to generate two tripentacyclic fused rings within the dithiasapphyrin framework. The resulting macrocycle adopts a highly distorted conformation, with the phenoxazine unit deviating by 66.97° from the mean plane defined by the four meso-carbon atoms. These doubly fused phenoxazine-embedded dithiasapphyrins exhibit intense panchromatic absorption across the UV–visible region with pronounced bathochromic shifts relative to their previously reported phenothiazine-fused analogues. Protonation with TFA further extends the absorption profile into the UV–visible-near-infrared region, affording strongly red-shifted diprotonated species. Electrochemical studies revealed that the phenoxazine-fused macrocycles are more electron-rich than the corresponding phenothiazine derivatives. Density functional theory and time-dependent density functional theory studies support the experimental observations.

item.title: Synthesis and Antiviral Evaluation of Sugar‐Modified Pseudouridine Analogs
item.description:
Sugar-modified nucleoside analogs of pseudouridine, which is a natural C-nucleoside, were synthesized. Antiviral screening identified weak to moderate inhibitors of Zika and dengue viruses (compounds 10, 11, 14, and 15). ProTide prodrugs of the lead compounds failed to enhance potency, suggesting that future work should focus on triphosphate analogs to investigate viral polymerase inhibition.


The pyrimidine C-nucleoside pseudouridine (Ψ) is a ubiquitous RNA modification that enhances the stability, modulates immunogenicity, and influences the biological function of natural and synthetic RNA. Despite its biological importance, the antiviral potential of pseudouridine analogs remains largely unexplored. Furthermore, although several sugar-modified pseudouridine analogs have been synthesized, a systematic approach to access these derivatives is still lacking. In this study, we present the synthesis of novel pseudouridine analogs with structural modifications at different positions of the carbohydrate moiety.

item.title: Synthetic Applications of Hypervalent Iodine Reagents in Multicomponent Reactions
item.description:
Hypervalent iodine reagents participate in and mediate diverse multicomponent reactions. This review highlights recent advances involving acyclic iodine(III) reagents, cyclic hypervalent iodine reagents, diaryliodonium salts, and iodine(V) reagents, with emphasis on their distinct activation modes and synthetic applications.


Multicomponent reactions (MCRs) provide an efficient strategy for the rapid assembly of structurally diverse molecules from simple starting materials in a one-pot manner. Meanwhile, hypervalent iodine reagents have emerged as versatile and environmentally benign reagents owing to their unique oxidative properties and diverse activation modes. The merger of hypervalent iodine chemistry with MCRs has enabled numerous efficient transformations involving oxidative activation, radical relay processes, electrophilic group transfer, and carbynoid chemistry. This review summarizes recent advances in hypervalent iodine-mediated MCRs involving acyclic iodine(III) reagents, cyclic hypervalent iodine reagents, diaryliodonium salts, and iodine(V) reagents.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Mediated Synthesis of Biscoumarins Utilizing Photocaged Sulfonic Acid as the Catalyst
item.description:
A mild visible light approach for the synthesis of biscoumarins utilizing arylazo sulfones as the photoacid generator under 467 nm irradiation is introduced.


Throughout the years, biscoumarin derivatives, known for their diverse biological properties, have attracted extensive synthetic interest. In pursuit of a sustainable, versatile, and cost-effective protocol, we studied the reaction between 4-hydroxycoumarin and various aldehydes, using arylazo sulfones as the photoacid generators. Hence, we developed a mild, visible-light-driven approach for the synthesis of biscoumarins, utilizing arylazo sulfones under 467 nm irradiation, affording products in moderate-to-high yields. The effectiveness and the limited waste production of our protocol, combined with its simplicity, including the purification by recrystallization, highlight its great potential for pharmaceutical applications.

item.title: Temperature‐Dependent Regiodivergent [3 + 2] Cycloaddition of Azomethine Ylides With (E)‐5‐Benzylidenethioxoimidazolidin‐4‐One
item.description:
An efficient route is developed to get access to novel dispiro[imidazolidine-4,1′-pyrrolo[2,1-a] isoquinoline-3′,3″-indoline]-2″,5-dione skeletons by a one-pot three-component [3 + 2] cycloaddition reaction of (E)-5-benzylidenethioxoimidazolidin-4-ones, isatin derivatives, and 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline (THIQ).


An efficient route is developed to gain access to novel dispiro[imidazolidine-4,1′-pyrrolo[2,1-a] isoquinoline-3′,3″-indoline]-2″,5-dione skeletons by a one-pot three-component [3 + 2] cycloaddition reaction of (E)-5-benzylidenethioxoimidazolidin-4-ones, isatin derivatives, and 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline. Interestingly we note that the reaction‘s regioselectivity depends on temperature, enabling the production of two regioisomericdispiro[imidazolidine-4,1′-pyrrolo[2,1-a] isoquinoline-3′,3″-indoline]-2″,5-dione in high yield. In agreement with the experimental results, density functional theory calculations carried out at the 6-31+g*(d,p)5 level of theory predicted that the [3 + 2] cycloaddition processes occur in an asynchronous concerted manner.

item.title: Solid‐State Melt Rearrangement/Acetylation Reaction of Primary Amides and PhI(OAc)2 in Reactive Eutectic Medium
item.description:
A substrates-involved reactive eutectic rearrangement/acetylation reaction from primary amides and PhI(OAc)2 without any solvents was developed. This reaction features lower temperature, shorter time, higher efficiency, and simpler operation.


A novel solid-state melt rearrangement reaction from primary amides and PhI(OAc)2 without any solvents in reactive eutectic medium was established. Compared with traditional solvent-involved or high-temperature solid-state reactions, this reaction features lower temperature, shorter time, and higher efficiency. Especially for the aliphatic diamides and PhI(OAc)2, they could easily form a reactive eutectic mixture and undergo double Hofmann-type rearrangement reactions, giving the diamine diacetylated products in high yields. Notably, the products can be easily isolated through a direct precipitation–filtration method.

item.title: c‐Met/DDR1 Dual‐Target Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Featuring an Imidazo[1,2‐A]pyridine Core
item.description:
In this contribution, we report a novel tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) based on bioisosteric replacement of cabozantinib’s pharmacophore fragment with an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine scaffold. The best compound, 10a, exhibited up to 2.6 μM IC50 against the cancer cell line HepG2. The inhibition selectivity profile assay demonstrated that 10a is a c-Met/DDR1 dual-target TKI.


In this contribution, we report the design, synthesis, and bioactivity evaluation of a novel class of dual-target tyrosine kinases inhibitors (TKIs). By linking imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines with a commonly used cyclopropanecarboxylic acid pharmacophore fragment, a number of novel potential TKIs were synthesized. Aryl and heteroaryl side chains with different electron-withdrawing groups and electron-donating groups were introduced to the imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine ring to evaluate the inhibitory effects against Huh-7 and HepG2 tumor cells. The research results showed that compound 10a with a pyridine side-chain exhibited better in vitro inhibitory effects against Huh-7 and HepG2 cells than cabozantinib. Cell cloning and cell scratch experiments indicated that 10a significantly hampered the tumor cell proliferation and migration and exhibited comparable cytotoxicity against normal cells. Through a selectivity profile study on a 217 kinase panel, cellular-mesenchymal epithelial transition factor (c-Met) and discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) were identified to be the potential targets of compound 10a.

item.title: HCo(PMe3)4‐Catalyzed 1,2‐Selective Hydroboration of Quinolines: Access to Isolable N–B and N–H 1,2‐Dihydroquinolines
item.description:
Well-defined cobalt hydride complexes are versatile catalysts. Two key features of HCo(PMe3)4 are that it promotes highly selective 1,2-hydroboration of quinolines to form N–B-substituted 1,2-dihydroquinolines (1,2-H-DHQs) under mild conditions, and that its volatile phosphine ligands and high solubility in pentane enable simple purification, allowing the isolation of stable N–B products that can be stored and be readily converted into N–H analogs.


Well-defined cobalt hydride complexes can be versatile catalysts that enable a wide range of transformations. In this work, we highlight two important aspects of the hydroboration of quinolines catalyzed by HCo(PMe3)4. First, we report its previously unexplored reactivity toward the highly selective 1,2-hydroboration of quinolines, providing direct access to N–B-substituted 1,2-dihydroquinolines (1,2-DHQs). This transformation proceeds efficiently under mild catalytic conditions and represents a selective route to partially reduced quinoline derivatives. Second, we demonstrate that the simplicity of HCo(PMe3)4, which contains volatile phosphine ligands and displays high solubility in pentane, enables a straightforward purification strategy for the resulting products. As a result, the N–B-protected 1,2-DHQs can be isolated in pure form, whereas they have previously been described mainly as crude intermediates. Importantly, these borylated compounds exhibit significantly improved stability over time compared to the corresponding N–H 1,2-DHQs, which are known to prone disproportionation pathway over time. The N–B derivatives can be readily stored and manipulated, making them convenient synthetic intermediates. Furthermore, they provide straightforward access to the corresponding N–H 1,2-DHQs through simple alcoholysis. This approach therefore offers a practical entry to otherwise unstorable N–H 1,2-dihydroquinolines and expands the synthetic utility of cobalt hydride catalysis in quinoline functionalization.

item.title: Anion‐Receptive Triazine‐Centered Azobenzene Trimers
item.description:
Triazine-centered azobenzene trimers combine visible-light switching and anion-responsive charge-transfer absorption in a single C 3-symmetric platform, establishing triazine scaffolds as versatile, multistimuli photoswitches for adaptive molecular and supramolecular materials.


Triazine-centered C 3-symmetric azobenzene trimers were synthesized using complementary azo-forming strategies, providing a versatile platform for multiresponsive molecular photoswitches. Relative to the isoelectronic benzonitrile monomer, incorporation of the triazine core induces an intrinsic bathochromic shift of the azobenzene absorption bands. The thiomethoxy-substituted derivative exhibits negative photochromism, enabling efficient trans–cis photoisomerization with wavelengths up to 525 nm. Combined temperature-dependent operando UV/vis spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal thermal cis–trans isomerization kinetics consistent with a triplet-assisted rotational pathway. Evaluation of transmission coefficients exposes pronounced solvent-friction effects, demonstrating that substituent-controlled solute–solvent coupling governs thermal half-lives beyond barrier heights. In addition, the electron-deficient triazine core enables anion binding that induces intramolecular charge-transfer absorption and modulates thermal relaxation, introducing triazine-centered azobenzenes as supramolecular multistimuli-responsive photoswitches.

item.title: Imide‐N‐Oxyl Radicals in the Synthesis of Functionalized Azocompounds From Azines via Challenging Radical Addition to C═N─N═C Fragment
item.description:
Oxidative free-radical coupling of azines and N-hydroxyimides with the formation of bis-(imide-N-oxy) azocompounds was discovered. The reaction takes place under mild metal-free conditions with PhI(OAc)2 as an oxidant. The synthesized azo compounds can serve as imide radical precursors.


Azines are easily available products of condensation between carbonyl compounds and hydrazine and at first glance look like perfect radical acceptors, azadienes. However, their free-radical chemistry is almost not developed due to relative inertness associated with the unusual behavior of the C═N─N═C fragment as a “conjugation stopper”. In the present work, the radical functionalization of azines by the addition of imide-N-oxyl radicals affording of bis-(imide-N-oxy) azocompounds is reported. The transformation proceeds through the generation of imide-N-oxyl radicals from N-hydroxyimides under room temperature and metal-free conditions. It is noteworthy that the addition of two equivalents of N-oxyl radicals occurs selectively, without the formation of products of hydrogen atom abstraction or other transformations of intermediate N, C-centered radicals (oxidation, dimerization, fragmentation, etc.). A broad range of ketazines and aldazines derived from aromatic and aliphatic carbonyl compounds are efficiently converted, demonstrating good functional-group tolerance. Notably, thermal decomposition of the NHPI-derived azo-ethers was found to generate phthalimide radicals. This work expands the radical chemistry of azines and provides a rare one-step approach to azo-ethers from readily accessible azines and N-hydroxyimides.

item.title: Isotelluroureas for Asymmetric C1 Ammonium Enolate Reactions
item.description:
Chiral isotelluroureas are powerful catalysts for a variety of C─C bond forming C1 ammonium enolate transformations.


Isotelluroureas (ITeUs) have recently been introduced as a novel class of highly nucleophilic Lewis base catalysts. Herein, we systematically screened them for their potential to facilitate C1 ammonium enolate transformations and directly compared them to their lighter chalcogen-analogs, the corresponding well-established isothioureas (ITUs) and isoselenoureas (ISeUs). We found ITeUs being well-suited for a variety of C1 ammonium enolate-based α-C─C bond forming reactions and in the majority of applications, the use of ITeUs allowed for significantly shorter reaction times compared to the use of ITUs or ISeUs, accompanied with often higher levels of enantioselectivities too.

item.title: Sc(OTf)3‐Catalyzed C3 Arylation and Sulfamidation of Imidazopyridine With Quinone Monoimines and p‐Quinone Diimides
item.description:
An operationally simple Sc(OTf)3-catalyzed CH arylation and sulfamidation of 2-arylimidazo[1,2-α]pyridines has been developed. This method exhibits excellent functional-group tolerance, and the products were obtained in good yields.


A simple and highly practical Sc(OTf)3-catalyzed CH arylation and sulfamidation of 2-arylimidazo[1,2-a]pyridines was developed. In this process, quinone monoimines and p-quinone diimides were employed as the arylating and sulfamidating reagents. The developed method demonstrates excellent regioselectivity, operational simplicity, and good substrate compatibility and the corresponding products were efficiently synthesized in 38%–90% yields.

item.title: Domino Synthesis of Furanyl‐1,2‐Diketones and One‐Pot Access to Furan‐Containing Quinoxalines
item.description:
Furanyl-1,2-diketones were efficiently synthesized through a copper-catalyzed domino process. Their transformation into furan-based quinoxalines was conveniently achieved by a one-pot protocol, highlighting a practical and versatile strategy for constructing heteroaromatic scaffolds of potential interest in synthetic and medicinal chemistry.


We report a domino protocol for the synthesis of furanyl 1,2-diketones from dialkynyl-1,6-diols. This one-step approach combines cyclization and oxidation, providing a streamlined and easy-to-perform synthetic route. The reaction has a broad substrate scope, accommodating both symmetrical and unsymmetrical 1,6-diols with various substituents on the aromatic rings. Consistently high regioselectivity is observed, according to the electronic properties of aromatics. Additionally, the method is successfully applied to the one-pot synthesis of substituted 2-(furan-2-yl)quinoxalines, demonstrating its utility in the rapid construction of complex heterocyclic structures.

item.title: Metal‐Free N‐Sulfonylation of Sulfoximines via Burgess Reagent and a CSI‐Enabled Four‐Component Strategy Toward Unsymmetric (Sulfoxylidene)Sulfamides
item.description:
A mild, metal-free, and additive-free N-sulfonylation of sulfoximines using Burgess reagent enables efficient synthesis of unsymmetric (sulfoxylidene)sulfamides. An operationally simple one-pot, four-component strategy further expands the scope to (sulfoxylidene)sulfamide–urea and related hybrids, highlighting the versatility and practicality of this approach.


Sulfamides and sulfoximines are valuable structural motifs in pharmaceutical and agrochemical research owing to their distinct physicochemical properties and biological significance. Herein, we report a mild, metal-free, and additive-free protocol for the N-sulfonylation of sulfoximines using Burgess reagent, for the first time, to afford unsymmetric (sulfoxylidene)sulfamides in good to excellent yields. Additionally, we report an operationally simple one-pot, four-component protocol that integrates chlorosulfonyl isocyanate (CSI), an alcohol, triethylamine, and a sulfoximine, which provides a significant alternative to the existing strategy. Replacing alcohols with amines or sulfoximines provides access to novel (sulfoxylidene)sulfamide–urea and (sulfoxylidene)sulfamide–(sulfoxylidene)urea hybrids, demonstrating the synthetic versatility of this methodology.

item.title: N‐Heteterocyclic Spiro‐Indenoid Frameworks Implemented Through [3 + 2]‐Spiro Annulation Involving Cyclic Ketimines and Alkynone or Its Structural Analog
item.description:
Generalized [3 + 2]-spiroannulation protocol allowing alkynone/alkynoate/alkynamide/alkynoic acid to interact regioselectively at the C2N1 bond of 2-arylquinoxalines and wide array of cyclic ketimines (quinoxalinone, benzoxazinone, benzimidazole, benzoxazole, and benzothiazole), implementing the synthesis of biologically relevant spirocyclic indene fused tetrasubstituted N-heterocyclic architechtures under mild reaction condition has been devised.


An efficient, atom-economic Ir(III) catalyzed [3 + 2]-spiroannulation has been devised, allowing alynone/alkynoate/alkynamide/alkynoic acid to interact regioselectively at the C2N1 bond rather than C3 N4 bond of 2-aryl quinoxaline and cyclic ketimines, thus implementing the synthesis of biologically relevant spirocyclic indene fused N-heterocyclic scaffolds under mild reaction condition. In silico studies have been attempted to predict the biological activity of the synthesized compounds involving computational target fishing strategy.

item.title: Development of a One‐Pot Borylation/Suzuki Cross‐Coupling Using Tetrahydroxydiboron en Route to Remibrutinib
item.description:
A one-pot borylation/Suzuki cross-coupling using tetrahydroxydiboron is developed for the synthesis of Remibrutinib (LOU064). The process combines low palladium catalyst loadings with methanol as a green solvent.


A one-pot borylation/Suzuki cross-coupling using tetrahydroxydiboron has been developed for the synthesis of the active pharmaceutical ingredient 6. This process is characterized by the utilization of remarkably low loadings of Pd-catalyst, the avoidance of pinacol hydrate precipitates in the final product, and the use of methanol as a green alcoholic solvent over both steps. This process is applied to Remibrutinib (LOU064) and addresses some of the previous problems associated with the use of bis(pinacolato)diboron as a borylating reagent, thus becoming a more atom-efficient and cost-effective approach.

item.title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Regioselective Cyclotrimerization of Terminal Alkynes to 1,3,5‐Trisubstituted Benzenes
item.description:
A synthetic strategy for the efficient construction of 1,3,5-trisubstituted benzene derivatives is reported via nickel-catalyzed regioselective cyclotrimerization of terminal alkynes. The reaction proceeds smoothly with Ni(dppf)Cl2 as catalyst and HBpin as additive, affording products in up to 84% yield. This transformation features mild conditions, easy operation, excellent regioselectivity, and high functional group tolerance. Preliminary mechanistic studies are conducted via isotope labeling experiments.


Herein, we report a synthetic strategy for the efficient construction of 1,3,5-trisubstituted benzene derivatives via nickel-catalyzed regioselective cyclotrimerization of terminal alkynes. The reaction proceeds smoothly employing Ni(dppf)Cl2 as the catalyst and pinacolborane (HBpin) as an additive, with the highest yield up to 84%. This transformation features mild conditions, easy operation, excellent regioselectivity, and high functional group tolerance. We conduct preliminary mechanistic studies via isotope labeling experiments.

item.title: Organocatalytic Stereoselective 1,10‐Conjugate Addition of Indole‐2‐Carboxylates to Alkynyl Aza‐2,4′‐Biphenyl Quinone Methides
item.description:
The stereocontrolled construction of axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes has been achieved through chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed 1,10-addition of indole-2-carboxylates to aza-2,4′-BQMs, which are generated in situ from α-[4-(2-aminophenyl)phenyl]propargyl alcohols.


Remote stereocontrolled functionalization plays a pivotal role in organic synthesis, particularly in the construction of chiral molecular frameworks. In this context, the organocatalytic remote conjugate addition to in situ generated conjugate systems derived from α-functionalized alcohols offers a robust synthetic strategy. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed 1,10-conjugate addition of indole-2-carboxylates to aza-2,4′-biphenyl quinone methides (aza-2,4′-BQMs), which are readily generated in situ from α-[4-(2-aminophenyl)phenyl]propargyl alcohols. This transformation enables the efficient construction of axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes in good yields and enantioselectivities. Importantly, this study not only broadens the scope of highly reactive aza-biphenyl quinone methides but also enriches the synthetic toolbox for enantioselective transformations involving aza-QMs.

item.title: Front Cover: HCo(PMe3)4‐Catalyzed 1,2‐Selective Hydroboration of Quinolines: Access to Isolable N–B and N–H 1,2‐Dihydroquinolines (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 31/2026)
item.description: The Front Cover shows that HCo(PMe3)4 promotes highly selective 1,2-hydroboration of quinolines to form N–B-substituted 1,2-dihydroquinolines. Its solubility in pentane enables simple purification, allowing the isolation of stable N–B products that can be stored over time and be converted into less stable N–H analogues by simple alcoholysis. More information can be found in the Research Article by C. C. Bories, M. Barbazanges, M. Petit and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70638). Cover art drawn by Emma El-Beaine (Sorbonne Université).

item.title: Photocatalytic Multicomponent Reactions: A Review of Recent Developments (2018–2025)
item.description:
This review highlights the transformative evolution of photocatalytic multicomponent reactions from 2018 to 2025. Driven by diverse activation modes—including single electron transfer, hydrogen atom transfer, energy transfer, and radical-polar crossover—this green synthetic paradigm enables the rapid, modular assembly of high-value molecular scaffolds and complex bioisosteres under mild conditions, addressing critical challenges in modern drug discovery.


Photocatalytic multicomponent reactions (PC-MCRs) have emerged as a transformative platform for the rapid assembly of structural complexity from simple precursors, perfectly aligning with the principles of green chemistry. This review provides a comprehensive update on the significant developments in this field from 2018 to 2025. Beyond a systematic overview of three-, four-, and pseudofive-component strategies, we critically examine the evolution of activation modes—ranging from single electron transfer (SET, a process involving the transfer of one electron between molecules to generate reactive radical intermediates) and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT, a concerted transfer of a proton and an electron to cleave inert CH bonds) to energy transfer (EnT, nonradiative energy transfer from excited photocatalysts to substrates without net electron exchange) and radical-polar crossover (RPCC, a sequential process converting radical intermediates to ionic species via electron transfer to achieve polarity reversal). Particular emphasis is placed on the modular synthesis of high-value scaffolds, including functionalized amines, pharmaceutically relevant heterocycles, and emerging bioisosteres like bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (BCPs). Furthermore, the paradigm shift toward sustainable synthesis, exemplified by the increasing use of metal-free dyes and heterogeneous semiconductors, is highlighted. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities, particularly regarding stereoselective control and industrial scalability, are discussed.

item.title: Recent Progress in the Synthesis of Entecavir
item.description:
Entecavir is a leading HBV DNA polymerase inhibitor for chronic hepatitis B. This review (2012–2025) classifies its total synthesis into three cyclopentane skeleton-building strategies, highlighting key features and offering valuable guidance for developing carbocyclic nucleoside analogs.


Entecavir, as the most effective hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA polymerase inhibitor currently used in the clinical treatment of chronic hepatitis B, holds significant clinical value. This paper systematically reviews the latest research advances (2012–2025) in the total synthesis of entecavir. Based on the differences in synthetic strategies for constructing its core cyclopentane skeleton, existing synthetic routes are categorized into three types: Carbon ring construction strategies mediated by cycloaddition and ring-closing metathesis, multi-catalytic cascade and fully catalytic asymmetric synthesis strategies, and stereoselective epoxide transformation and tandem reaction strategies. This classification not only clearly presents the technical characteristics of different synthetic approaches but also provides an important reference for the development of carbocyclic nucleoside analogs.

item.title: Harnessing Electron Donor–Acceptor Complexes for Functionalization of Unsaturated Hydrocarbons
item.description:
This review focuses on olefins and alkynes as substrates in photochemical reactions, highlighting their roles in photocatalytic transformations via EDA complex formation, including CC, CN, and CS bond formations.


Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes have long been known to facilitate numerous photocatalytic organic transformations. Recently, alkene and alkyne derivatives have emerged as robust coupling partners in EDA complex-driven photocatalytic reactions, leading to the formation of important molecules. Upon irradiation, the EDA complex undergoes an intramolecular single-electron transfer (SET), generating radicals that play a crucial role in driving the reaction without requiring any external photocatalyst. This sustainable complex photochemistry has become an atom-economical and advantageous strategy for synthesizing numerous biologically active molecules containing olefin and alkyne frameworks. Recently, significant progress has been made in this field, particularly in the transformation of readily accessible alkynes and alkenes into a wide range of CC and CX (X = N, S, etc.) bonds. We believe a detailed literature review on this specific topic would significantly benefit researchers engaged in photocatalytic functionalization of alkynes and olefins, particularly the mechanistic advancements reported over the past 5 years.

item.title: π‐Extended Silyl Enolates as Emerging Platforms in Radical Chemistry
item.description:
This review covers the emerging role of π-extended silyl polyenol ethers in radical chemistry. It highlights their versatile roles as electron-rich SOMOphiles, silyl radical cation precursors, and nucleophilic partners in radical–polar crossover manifolds, while considering recent advances in photoredox catalysis, electrochemistry, and transition metal-mediated (M+) methodologies.


π-Extended silyl polyenol ethers and their related silyl ketene acetals are well-established vinylogous nucleophiles in polar transformations; however, their potential in radical chemistry has only recently emerged. Owing to their intrinsically electron-rich character, arising from conjugated π-systems and σ-donating silyl groups, these substrates display unique reactivity under single-electron transfer conditions. This review provides a comprehensive overview of their behavior in radical-mediated processes, highlighting their versatile role as electron-rich SOMOphiles, radical precursors, and nucleophilic partners in radical–polar crossover manifolds. A key concept underlying their reactivity is the umpolung induced by single-electron oxidation, which converts nucleophilic vinylogous enolates into electrophilic radical cation or keto-allyl radical intermediates, thereby unlocking unconventional bond-forming pathways inaccessible through traditional two-electron chemistry. Moreover, these systems exhibit a distinctive propensity for remote functionalization at γ-, ε-, and η-positions, governed by electronic delocalization and radical stabilization across the extended π-framework. Recent advances in photoredox catalysis, electrochemistry, and transition metal-mediated methodologies have significantly expanded the scope and synthetic utility of these transformations, enabling efficient C─C and C─heteroatom bond formation, enantioselective variants, and applications in the synthesis of complex molecules. Collectively, these developments position π-extended silyl polyenol ethers as versatile and tunable platforms in modern radical chemistry.

item.title: A Straightforward Synthesis of Benzestrol by Matteson Homologation Using Chiral Benzyl Carbamates
item.description:
Benzestrol can easily be obtained stereoselectively via Matteson reaction using chiral Boronic esters and chiral benzyl carbamates.


A straightforward and highly stereoselective synthesis of the non-steroidal estrogen benzestrol is described based on Matteson homologations. Starting from a chiral arylboronic ester two classical Matteson reactions allow the introduction of two stereogenic centers, while the third one is transferred from a chiral benzyl carbamate under retention. Protodeboration and deprotection provide benzestrol in only 6 steps and an overall yield of 30%.

item.title: Sunscreens as Organic Energy Materials: Macroscopic Heat Release Through Vibrational Relaxation Mechanism
item.description:
We show for the first time that ACHI derivatives can effectively convert UV and sunlight into heat in solid coatings, raising temperatures by up to 15 °C. These transparent materials are durable under prolonged UV exposure and work best when applied as uniform thin films. Their efficient light-to-heat conversion makes them promising candidates for smart windows and other energy-management technologies.


Aminocyclohexenimine (ACHI) derivatives are powerful UV-absorbing molecules, long recognized for their unique properties as sunscreens. Here, we demonstrate for the first time the macroscopic heat release through the previously proposed vibrational relaxation mechanism at the molecular level. Thin films of four different ACHI derivatives deposited on quartz substrates produced measurable macroscopic temperature increases (up to 15 °C) under UV and simulated solar irradiation and moderate-to-excellent photothermal stability (maximum half-life of 116 h under continuous UV). While drop-cast films provided proof of concept, spin coating yielded transparent and homogeneous layers that enabled direct monitoring of both thermal and spectroscopic responses in the solid state. These experiments revealed that solid-state absorption spectra, rather than solution-phase properties, correlate best with photothermal performance. The combination of transparency, durability, and efficient light-to-heat conversion highlights ACHI derivatives as a pioneering family of organic photothermal coatings, with potential applications in energy-managing and optically transparent technologies such as smart windows.

item.title: Competing Charge Transport Pathways: A Spirobifluorene‐Based Molecular Loop
item.description:
